spans.text: Read the through-line first. Each chapter then opens with where it sits in the argument, before its approved notes, and the connections close the loop.
What is the stock here, and which flows change it?

parts.title: Watch the stock, not the event

spans.text: The book asks you to watch stocks before you watch the events that fill them, because a stock is the memory the flows write.

parts.title: The level moves only by the difference

spans.text: This is where the through-line's stock first appears, as a bathtub: the level changes only as fast as the inflow and the outflow differ.

blocks.title: Watch for this in the notes

spans.text: Events are the flows. The thing you can point at tomorrow is the stock.
The bathtub is not a metaphor the book leaves behind: every later loop is the same stock, with the flows tied back to it.
